To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a Bayesian adaptive design for personalized Phase I cancer clinical trials that utilizes all toxicities and patient biomarker information to estimate a personalized maximum tolerated dose.
we have proposed a Bayesian adaptive Phase 1 design which can estimate personalized maximum tolerated doses based on all toxicities and genomic profiles.

a new Bayesian adaptive Phase I cancer trial design that utilizes biomarkers in the estimation of personalized maximum tolerated dose is proposed and the design operating characteristic is evaluated with extensive simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new methodology to incorporate patient biomarkers to estimate pMTDs for cancer Phase I clinical trials.
the development and evaluation of a novel Bayesian adaptive Phase I clinical trial model for estimating pMTDs by incorporating patient biomarker information.
the development of a new cancer Phase I trial design with inclusion of biomarker information in estimating pMTD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our novel cancer Phase I trial designs with inclusion of biomarker(s) can improve the efficiency and accuracy of personalized MTD estimation and have the potential to increase the therapeutic effect of cancer drug treatment.

our novel cancer Phase I design with inclusion of covariates in the EWOC model is useful for estimating personalized MTD and has the substantial potential to improve treatment outcomes for patients with cancer.
our proposed Bayesian adaptive Phase I designs can estimate a personalized maximum tolerated dose by utilizing patient biomarker information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of biomarkers into the EWOC-NETs model can improve the estimation of pMDT and the estimation of the probability of response to the drug.
we developed a new cancer phase I design with biomarkers to improve the accuracy of pMTD estimation.
our proposed designs can be used to estimate pMTDs for cancer therapeutic agents by utilizing biomarker information to improve the accuracy of pMTD estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed methodology can improve the estimation of pMDT while maintaining the original advantages of the EWOC-NETs design.

the use of biomarkers in Phase I clinical trial designs can improve the accuracy of pMTD estimation and thus increase the therapeutic effect of the novel cancer therapeutic agents for individual patients.
biomarkers that are predictive of toxicity and efficacy of cancer treatment can be incorporated to improve the efficiency of Phase I trials.
